original_value: AbstractWe describe punctual categoricity in several natural classes, including binary relational structures and mono-unary functional structures. We prove that every punctually categorical structure in a finite unary language is${\text {PA}}(0')$-categorical, and we show that this upper bound is tight. We also construct an example of a punctually categorical structure whose degree of categoricity is$0''$. We also prove that, with a bit of work, the latter result can be pushed beyond$\Delta ^1_1$, thus showing that punctually categorical structures can possess arbitrarily complex automorphism orbits.As a consequence, it follows that binary relational structures and unary structures are not universal with respect to primitive recursive interpretations; equivalently, in these classes every rich enough interpretation technique must necessarily involve unbounded existential quantification or infinite disjunction. In contrast, it is well-known that both classes are universal for Turing computability.

result.paraphrase: We examine punctual categoricity in several natural settings, including binary relational and mono-unary functional structures. We prove that any punctually categorical structure in a finite unary language is ${\text {PA}}(0')$-categorical, and we show this bound is optimal. We also build an example of a punctually categorical structure with degree of categoricity $0''$. In addition, with some extra work, the latter phenomenon can be extended beyond $\Delta ^1_1$, demonstrating that punctually categorical structures may have arbitrarily complicated automorphism orbits. As a consequence, binary relational structures and unary structures are not universal for primitive recursive interpretations; equivalently, in these classes any sufficiently rich interpretation method must use unbounded existential quantification or infinite disjunction. By contrast, it is well known that both classes are universal for Turing computability.
